mbm-1226.clue: My bass line started with a loose screw.
mbm-1226.quote: Our practice amp buzzed on one particular note. I played a little answer to the buzz while we waited for a screwdriver. The amp is fixed and the answer is still in our chorus.

mbm-1227.quote: At camp a moth kept casting a giant shadow across the tent. We lowered the lantern and draped a towel as a stage curtain. The moth had a very distinguished second career in shadow theater.

mbm-1228.clue: I let a leaf sign my work.
mbm-1228.quote: I rolled a real fern into the side of a clay cylinder and peeled it off before firing. Every vein stayed. I use the pot for my pencils and save the fern’s finest line for myself.

mbm-1229.clue: I quilt a jacket for every jar.
mbm-1229.quote: Our jam bottles travel inside padded sleeves from my quilting scraps. At the family fair the apricot jam sold out first. Three people asked how much I wanted for the coat it arrived in.

mbm-1230.clue: I keep half a plastic trophy.
mbm-1230.quote: My best friend and I tied in the local dumpling contest. The prize was a little plastic bowl that came apart at the base. He keeps the bowl, I keep the stem, and we reunite them for dinner.

mbm-1231.clue: I’m the person rustling the leaves.
mbm-1231.quote: For the forest scene I used a paper bag full of dried leaves at the side of the stage. One leaf floated into the spotlight and the lead caught it without missing a line. We kept the catch.

mbm-1232.clue: I made a quilt with a bus route.
mbm-1232.quote: I laid out a line of colored rectangles for every bus stop to my aunt’s house. The last stop is a scrap of her kitchen curtain and a tiny embroidered cake. I always take the full route.

mbm-1233.clue: I wrote a program for our fish.
mbm-1233.quote: A little pixel fish follows the cursor across my monitor. I showed my nephew how to change its color. By supper it had seven different fins and the most alarming purple smile.

mbm-1234.clue: I never throw the striped one first.
mbm-1234.quote: I sewed one juggling bag from an old striped sock, and it flies a little slower than the others. If I throw it last I get enough time to wink at the front row.

mbm-1235.clue: I let the willow comb my hat.
mbm-1235.quote: The little creek is just broad enough for my kayak. I float under the willow and let the fine branches brush my brim. At home I usually find one leaf tucked beside the band.

mbm-1236.clue: I made a sunset you can button.
mbm-1236.quote: I used five mismatched orange buttons down the front of a blouse, darkest at the hem. My sister put it on at the window and lined herself up with the actual sunset.

mbm-1237.clue: My vase has an unexpected spout.
mbm-1237.quote: I pinched one side of the rim while lifting my new pot. When it came out of the kiln I tried pouring water. It makes a perfect thin stream for the smallest plant on my sill.

mbm-1238.clue: I let the shadow take the practice swing.
mbm-1238.quote: On our evening round my uncle’s shadow reaches halfway to my ball. He swings first, then I try to follow the shadow through. He says it’s the tallest he’s felt in years.

mbm-1239.clue: Our club has a mirror for shoes.
mbm-1239.quote: The disco mirror cracked years ago and its last good strip sits along the baseboard. We practice our footwork in it. Sometimes I know who’s arrived by their shoes a whole song before I see their face.

mbm-1240.clue: I paddled through a field of blue.
mbm-1240.quote: At the end of our rafting trip the river slowed beside a bank full of blue flowers. Their reflection climbed all the way up the wet side of the raft. I held the paddle still for one bend.

mbm-1241.clue: I camp with a tiny red postbox.
mbm-1241.quote: My friends and I put a red biscuit tin outside the tent for notes. On the last night somebody had left a drawing of our camp under the stars. The postbox came home very carefully.

mbm-1242.clue: I drew a map of the dragon’s belly.
mbm-1242.quote: I crawled beside the mini-golf dragon to see where the ball came out. My niece drew a dotted line over my sketch from its teeth to its tail. It’s our official course guide now.

mbm-1243.clue: I keep the tiniest scarf warm.
mbm-1243.quote: I made a scarf too short even for a doll. It fit around the neck of my wooden spoon. That spoon stands on our counter looking ready for cold soup.

mbm-1244.clue: I taught my hat to sneer.
mbm-1244.quote: A pair of paper eyebrows on elastic turns my magic hat into a grumpy assistant. When a silk scarf gets stuck I pull one eyebrow up. The hat always gets a bigger laugh than the scarf.

mbm-1245.quote: I hold a paper star in the afternoon sun and let its shadow cross somebody’s open palm. The trick ends with a little foil star already in their hand. My favorite part is watching their fingers close.

mbm-1246.clue: I only meant to buy the frame.
mbm-1246.quote: An old frame at the market held a faded drawing of a pear. Once I hung it, the pear looked so content I couldn’t bring myself to replace it. Now I buy fresh pears to keep it company.

mbm-1247.clue: I registered under my real name this time.
mbm-1247.quote: My cousin entered me in the corn contest as Captain Butter. I ate two ears and spent the afternoon signing napkins. Next year I brought a captain’s hat just for the photographs.

mbm-1248.quote: I tried sketching passing freight cars on a long roll of drawing paper. A little girl at the station joined me halfway through, so the last six blue wagons are twice as tall as the first seven.

mbm-1249.clue: I keep the chalk line on the inside.
mbm-1249.quote: I made my first pair of trousers with my uncle, who marked the hem with blue tailor’s chalk. A little mark survived the wash. It peeks out whenever I cuff them for a walk.

mbm-1250.clue: My pajama pocket holds the prediction.
mbm-1250.quote: For our Friday show we each hide a suspect’s name in a pocket. Once my pocket carried the right guess and two peppermints. I tipped them all onto the table for a very sweet victory.
